name: crontab
description: Schedules recurring commands: each user has their own crontab of cron expressions and jobs.

flags.description: Remove ALL your jobs (no undo — use -e and delete lines instead).
Operate on another user's crontab (root only).

examples.explanation: Opens your crontab in the editor. Add lines like the examples below and save.
Runs backup.sh every day at 03:00. The five fields: minute hour day month weekday.
Every 15 minutes, logging output. ALWAYS redirect cron output — otherwise results are emailed/lost.

about: Cron reads /var/spool/cron/ (per user) and /etc/cron.d/. Environment in cron is minimal: PATH is usually /usr/bin:/bin, so ALWAYS use absolute paths for executables and files. Special strings exist: @daily, @hourly, @weekly, @reboot. Cron does not run jobs missed while the machine was off (anacron does).
mistakes: Forgetting absolute paths — cron's PATH is minimal and scripts fail silently.
Not redirecting output; errors vanish into mail nobody reads.
Using % in cron commands unescaped — % is special in crontab; escape as \%.
warnings: crontab -r deletes everything with no confirmation. Check crontab -l before and after any edit.
distroNotes: Standard cron (vixie-cron) on Debian/Ubuntu; cronie on RHEL-family adds anacron features. systemd timers are the modern alternative with logging and dependencies.
